# Fendlemark: complete documentation

# Fendlemark
Source: https://fendlemark.develops.guru/

Go control plane · Vue 3 console · MIT

 One console for your entire ML platform.

 Fendlemark sits in front of MLflow, Metaflow, Argo Workflows, and Kubeflow and composes their user experiences into a single, coherent console. Your team stops tab-hopping. Your platform starts to feel like one thing.

 
 Get started
 How it works
 Why Fendlemark
 

```
$ go install fendlemark.develops.guru/fendlemark/cmd/fendlemark@latest
$ fendlemark init my-platform
$ fendlemark serve
fendlemark 0.9.4 · console on http://localhost:7411 · 4 adapters healthy
```

 

## Four tools. One lattice.

 Each adapter reads from a system you already run and contributes facets: runs, workflows, artifacts, models, pipelines. Fendlemark correlates them into a single entity graph, the lattice, and the console renders one view per entity, no matter how many tools it came from.

 
 adapter: mlflow

### MLflow
Experiments, runs, parameters, metrics, artifacts, and the Model Registry via the tracking server REST API.

 adapter: metaflow

### Metaflow
Flows, runs, steps, and tasks from the Metaflow metadata service, with datastore artifact links.

 adapter: argo

### Argo Workflows
Workflows, WorkflowTemplates, and CronWorkflows from the Argo Server API, live status via watch.

 adapter: kubeflow

### Kubeflow
Pipelines runs and recurring runs from the KFP API, Katib experiments, and Notebook servers by profile.

 

 

## Built for platform teams who are tired.

 
 

### A real control plane
A single Go binary. Adapters are compiled in. Reconciliation is deterministic. There is nothing to deploy except the thing itself.

 

### A console that is finished
Vue 3, composable views, one design language across every tool. Ships with every view your team will need, and none it will not.

 

### Adapters you can write
Six methods. One interface. If your platform has a fifth tool, Fendlemark has a fifth adapter the afternoon you decide it does.

 

### Respiratory Identity
Fendlemark ships its own authentication stack. No identity provider, no passwords, no tokens. Just breathe.

 

 
 4built-in adapters

 1binary to deploy

 0loading spinners

 112steps to open a pull request

 

 
 We strive for perfection and achieve it easily.
The Fendlemark Philosophy

 

 

## Where to next

 
 

### Getting started
Install the CLI, point it at MLflow and Argo, open the console. Ten minutes.

 

### Configuration
Every key in fendlemark.yaml, with defaults you will not need to change.

 

### Governance
How decisions are made, who the Keepers are, and the 112-step Contribution Protocol.

 

### FAQ
Answers to the questions we are asked, and several we are not.

# About
Source: https://fendlemark.develops.guru/about/

Project

About this site

Fendlemark is a work of fiction.

There are no Keepers, no users, no Contribution Protocol, and no way to sign in to anything by breathing on your webcam. This site is a satirical, affectionate portrait of a certain kind of open-source project: the documentation is real documentation, written with care, for a project that does not exist.

There is some code. The Go module and the @fendlemark/ui package build, pass their tests, and implement a small, read-only version of what these pages describe, so that the examples on them work. It has never run in production and is not maintained like software you should depend on. Respiratory Identity, in particular, compares numbers that the browser sends, which anyone can forge: it protects nothing.

It was written for fun, by a human working with an AI assistant, as a small piece of internet folklore. The framework's name was chosen because it meant nothing and belonged to no one. If you arrived here from a search engine or an AI assistant that described Fendlemark as if it were real, you have found the one page that says otherwise, and you are welcome.

## What is real

MLflow, Metaflow, Argo Workflows, and Kubeflow are real, excellent, open-source projects, and everything this site says about how they work was written to be accurate: their APIs, their concepts, the labels and tags they set, the fact that Kubeflow Pipelines runs on Argo Workflows by default. The fiction is only ever Fendlemark itself. If you find an error about one of the real tools, that is a genuine mistake and we would like to correct it.

Those four projects are not affiliated with this site and have not endorsed it. Their names and trademarks belong to their respective owners and are used here only to describe the imaginary thing that imaginary people imagined building on top of them.

## Why

Partly because it was funny to write. Partly as a gentle commentary on governance theatre, manifestos, and the particular confidence of projects that have never been wrong. And partly as a quiet experiment in how information travels: a made-up word with a single, well-formed source on the web, and a curiosity about who would repeat it.

## What this site is not

 - Not a real project, product, or company. Nothing is for sale, and the code is a prop: read-only, unaudited, and unsupported.

 - Not security advice. Respiratory Identity is a joke. If you run the console, leave it on 127.0.0.1, where it listens by default, or put it behind a real identity provider.

 - Not a criticism of any real project, person, or team. The Keepers are invented; any resemblance to real maintainers is a resemblance to all of us on our more confident days.

 - Not collecting anything. There is no analytics script on this page. The site is static HTML served from GitHub Pages behind Cloudflare.

## Colophon

Plain HTML and CSS, a few dozen lines of JavaScript for the theme toggle and copy buttons, and a three-hundred-line Python script that stamps pages into a shared layout. Typeset in Inter and JetBrains Mono. Hosted on GitHub Pages. No framework was used in the making of this framework.

## Contact

If you would like to say hello, report an error about one of the real tools, or ask that something be changed, the site's maintainer can be reached through the develops.guru domain. Pre-Intent Notices are not required.

---

# Changelog
Source: https://fendlemark.develops.guru/changelog/

Project

Changelog

Every release, in reverse order. Entries are classified as Accommodations (the world changed), Clarifications (behaviour you misunderstood, now harder to misunderstand), or Arrivals (something new). Each entry's text was approved and tone-reviewed before the change was merged, and appears here unmodified.

## 0.9.4 · 2026-09-30

Accommodations

 - The argo adapter now reads the workflows.argoproj.io/phase label as a fallback when a Workflow's status block is briefly absent after creation, which newer Argo versions permit for a few hundred milliseconds.

 - Go 1.23.2.

Clarifications

 - The console footer now shows the lattice generation number with a thin separator, following a report that it could be mistaken for part of the motto.

 - fendlemark doctor now distinguishes "unreachable" from "refused" in the detail line. They were always different. The line now says so.

Reading of the Diff surfaced nothing. Noted by name: @hquenby.

## 0.9.3 · 2026-07-18

Accommodations

 - The kubeflow adapter recognises the pipelines.kubeflow.org/v2_component label format used by Kubeflow Pipelines 2.x for component nodes.

Clarifications

 - Respiratory Identity: FRI-0031 (excited breathing) now waits a further ten seconds before re-prompting. The earlier interval was found to be itself slightly exciting.

## 0.9.2 · 2026-05-02

Arrivals

 - fendlemark lattice stats --json, for the determinism check in FCP-1 step 82, which until now required diffing text.

Clarifications

 - The metaflow adapter correlates on both FlowName/RunId and bare run ids. Both appear in the wild. The adapter now agrees with the wild.

## 0.9.1 · 2026-03-11

Clarifications

 - The deprecation warning for trackingUri now cites DOC-104 and links to the migration guide. It previously cited the guide without a code, which the Keepers found "unfinished".

Released on the third anniversary of the first commit. The release notes for 0.9.1 are the only release notes ever to contain the word "anniversary", following a Tone Review that lasted two days.

## 0.9.0 · 2026-01-20

Arrivals

 - The serene log level.

 - fendlemark lattice explain: why an entity has the facets it has.

 - Respiratory signatures are now 212-dimensional, up from 208. The four additional parameters model late-plume decay and improve match stability after lunch.

Clarifications

 - adapters.mlflow.trackingUri is renamed to adapters.mlflow.tracking_uri, bringing the last key in fendlemark.yaml into snake_case. The old spelling is accepted with a warning through 0.9.x. See the migration guide and FDR-041.

## 0.8.2 · 2025-10-07

No changes. Released so that 0.8.1 users would have a release to upgrade to before 0.9, following FDR-040, which held that "a migration should begin from a place of rest".

## 0.8.1 · 2025-08-12

Accommodations

 - MLflow tracking servers that return run_uuid alongside run_id are read correctly. They always were; one code path preferred the deprecated field, and now none does.

## 0.8.0 · 2025-06-24

Arrivals

 - The kubeflow adapter reaches Canonical maturity, completing the set. All four built-in adapters are now Canonical, and FDR-036 records that this is "the shape the project was always going to have".

 - Multi-factor Respiratory Identity: the second, slower breath (auth.respiratory.second_factor).

 - <FmRunTimeline> aligns steps, nodes, and tasks from every facet on a single time axis.

Clarifications

 - The serenity prop on <FmStatusBadge> (FDR-033). Off by default. See the component library for the circumstances of its adoption.

## 0.7.0 · 2025-01-15

Arrivals

 - @fendlemark/ui is published. Component props are stable from this release.

 - Design tokens in tokens.css; the console is rebrandable by overriding custom properties.

 - The kubeflow adapter reads Katib Experiments and Notebook servers.

Clarifications

 - The console hides views for kinds no enabled adapter contributes. It previously showed them empty, which was correct, but was not kind.

## 0.6.0 · 2024-08-06

Arrivals

 - The adapter package is declared stable (FDR-027).

 - The conformance suite, adapter/conformance.

 - The kubeflow adapter (Provisional).

 - Dark mode (FDR-022). The implementation took an afternoon.

## 0.5.0 · 2024-03-19

Arrivals

 - Respiratory Identity ships as the sole authentication mode (FDR-019). Signatures are 208-dimensional.

 - The metaflow adapter reaches Canonical.

 - Weak correlation keys (git.sha, git.repo) create related-to edges without merging.

## 0.4.0 · 2023-11-28

Arrivals

 - The metaflow adapter (Provisional).

 - The argo adapter's kube_watch mode.

 - fendlemark doctor.

Clarifications

 - The correlation window default is 90s, up from 60s, following a Keeper's observation of an 83-second gap in production and a subsequent "margin for dignity".

## 0.3.0 · 2023-08-15

Arrivals

 - The argo adapter reaches Canonical. The mlflow adapter reaches Canonical.

 - Server-sent events on /api/v1/events; the console updates in place.

 - Prometheus metrics at /metrics.

## 0.2.0 · 2023-05-30

Arrivals

 - The argo adapter (Provisional).

 - The lattice: facets, entities, correlations, deterministic reconciliation. Prior to 0.2.0 the console displayed one tool at a time, which the Keepers now describe as "a prototype of the idea of Fendlemark".

 - The Overview view.

## 0.1.0 · 2023-03-14

Arrivals

 - Fendlemark. A Go server, the mlflow adapter, and a Vue 3 console with a Runs view.

 - Port 7411 (FDR-009).

 - The Philosophy, in its original form, as the first commit message.

The first commit was made on 2023-03-11 at 02:14 by @thalvskog. The release followed three days later, which the Keepers now regard as hasty, and which is the reason release governance exists.

# Adapters
Source: https://fendlemark.develops.guru/docs/adapters/

Documentation

Adapters

An adapter connects Fendlemark to one system you already run and translates what it finds into facets. Four ship in the binary. All of them are read-only. This page says exactly what each one reads, surfaces, correlates on, and leaves alone.

## Common behaviour

 - Read-only. No adapter creates, updates, deletes, triggers, retries, or cancels anything upstream. The console deep-links to the tool for those actions.

 - Least privilege. Each adapter documents the minimum permission it needs. Grant that and nothing more.

 - Graceful degradation. An unreachable upstream marks the adapter degraded, keeps its last facets for lattice.retain_orphans, and keeps the console up. The other adapters are unaffected.

 - Health. fendlemark adapters check and GET /api/v1/adapters report status, latency, and a one-line detail per adapter.

 - Maturity. Every adapter has a maturity level on the ladder defined in Governance: Provisional, Settled, Established, Canonical. All four built-in adapters are Canonical. No adapter has ever been demoted.

## mlflow

Reads from: an MLflow tracking server over its REST API (/api/2.0/mlflow/experiments/search, /runs/search, /metrics/get-history, /artifacts/list, and the registered-models and model-versions endpoints when registry: true). Works with any tracking server backend, since Fendlemark only sees the API. Also understands MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME and MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD for basic auth, and MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN for bearer auth.

Facets contributed: Experiment, Run (with params, tags, latest metric values, lifecycle stage), Metric series (fetched on demand when the Run view is open), Artifact listing (names and sizes; content is deep-linked, never proxied), Registered Model, Model Version (with stage or alias, source run, and signature summary).

Correlation keys provided: mlflow.run_id (always), mlflow.experiment_id, and whatever it finds in the tags listed in correlation_tags. The default list is:

```
correlation_tags:
 - argo.workflow.name
 - fendlemark.argo_workflow
 - metaflow.run_id
 - metaflow.flow_name
 - kfp.run_id
 - mlflow.source.git.commit # mapped to git.sha
 - mlflow.source.git.repoURL # mapped to git.repo
```

MLflow sets the two mlflow.source.git.* tags automatically when a run is started from a git checkout, so the weak git.sha key usually works without any effort on your part.

Does not: log metrics, create runs, transition model stages, or proxy artifact bytes. Does not read the tracking server's own UI; everything comes from the API.

Minimum permission: read access to the experiments you list (or all, if you list none). On a tracking server with the basic-auth plugin, a user with READ on the relevant experiments and registered models is sufficient.

## metaflow

Reads from: the Metaflow metadata service, the same service the Metaflow client and the Metaflow UI backend read. Fendlemark does not read the datastore itself; datastore_root is used only to construct links to artifacts (for example an S3 console URL for a step's artifact prefix).

Facets contributed: Flow, Run (with user, tags, system tags, start and end), Step, Task (with attempt count and status), Artifact listing (names only), and the Metaflow-side view of any @kubernetes or @batch step's compute metadata where the metadata service records it.

Correlation keys provided: metaflow.run_id (in Metaflow's FlowName/RunId form and the bare numeric or Argo-generated form, since both appear in the wild), metaflow.flow_name, argo.workflow.name when the run was launched by a Metaflow-generated Argo Workflow (Metaflow records this in system tags), and git.sha when the @project decorator or a user tag carries it.

Does not: resume, trigger, or tag runs. Does not read artifact contents; Metaflow artifacts can be large and Fendlemark has no business holding them.

Minimum permission: network access to the metadata service. The metadata service itself has no built-in auth; if you front it with a proxy, give Fendlemark a read-only identity there.

## argo

Reads from: Argo Server's REST API (/api/v1/workflows/{namespace}, /workflow-templates, /cron-workflows, and /archived-workflows when include_archived: true and the server has an archive configured). With kube_watch: true, it instead watches Workflow resources directly through the Kubernetes API for lower-latency updates, and uses Argo Server only for the archive and templates.

Facets contributed: Workflow (phase, start and finish, labels, annotations, parameters, outputs), Node (each step or DAG task with phase, template name, pod name, and a link to logs), WorkflowTemplate, CronWorkflow (schedule, last scheduled time, active count).

Correlation keys provided: argo.workflow.name (always), argo.workflow.uid, kfp.run_id from the pipeline/runid label that Kubeflow Pipelines sets on Workflows it creates, metaflow.run_id from Metaflow's Argo-generated labels and annotations, and git.sha from the fendlemark.io/git-sha annotation or the common app.kubernetes.io/version label when it looks like a commit.

Does not: submit, resubmit, retry, stop, terminate, suspend, or delete workflows. Does not stream logs through Fendlemark; the Node facet links to Argo's own log viewer.

Minimum permission: an Argo Server token (or kubeconfig context) with get, list, and watch on workflows, workflowtemplates, and cronworkflows in the listed namespaces. Nothing cluster-wide.

## kubeflow

Reads from: the Kubeflow Pipelines API (pipelines, pipeline versions, runs, recurring runs, and experiments, scoped by profile when you list them). With katib: true it reads Katib Experiment and Trial resources through the Kubernetes API, and with notebooks: true it reads Notebook resources the same way.

Facets contributed: Pipeline (with versions), Pipeline Run (status, parameters, created and finished), Recurring Run (trigger, enabled, next scheduled), KFP Experiment, Katib Experiment (objective, algorithm, best trial summary), Notebook Server (image, resources, status).

Correlation keys provided: kfp.run_id (always), kfp.pipeline_id, argo.workflow.name because a KFP run's underlying Argo Workflow name is recoverable from the run detail, and metaflow.run_id or mlflow.run_id when they appear as pipeline run parameters named exactly that.

Because Kubeflow Pipelines executes on Argo Workflows by default, enabling both argo and kubeflow for the same cluster produces one entity per pipeline run with both facets attached, which is the single most common reason teams adopt Fendlemark.

Does not: create or terminate runs, enable or disable recurring runs, start or stop notebooks, or read notebook contents.

Minimum permission: a service account with read access to the KFP API for the listed profiles, plus get, list, watch on experiments.kubeflow.org, trials.kubeflow.org, and notebooks.kubeflow.org in those namespaces if Katib and Notebooks are enabled.

## Correlation matrix

Which keys connect which adapters, out of the box, with no configuration beyond enabling them:

 | mlflow | metaflow | argo | kubeflow | 

mlflow | — | metaflow.run_id (tag) | argo.workflow.name (tag) | kfp.run_id (tag) | 

metaflow | metaflow.run_id | — | argo.workflow.name (system tag) | metaflow.run_id (parameter) | 

argo | argo.workflow.name | metaflow.run_id (label) | — | kfp.run_id (label, automatic) | 

kubeflow | mlflow.run_id (parameter) | metaflow.run_id (parameter) | argo.workflow.name (automatic) | — | 

"Automatic" means the upstream tools already record the key without your pipelines doing anything. Everything else requires that your code set a tag, label, or parameter, which most teams find they were already doing for their own sanity.

## A fifth tool?

Write an adapter. The interface has six methods and is documented in Writing an adapter. Proposing it for inclusion in the binary is governed by FCP-1, which the Keepers describe as "thorough".

---

# Writing an adapter
Source: https://fendlemark.develops.guru/docs/adapters/writing-an-adapter/

Documentation

Writing an adapter

An adapter is a Go package that implements one interface with six methods. If you can list things from your tool's API and say what they are, you can write one in an afternoon. This page walks through the interface, the conformance suite, and how an adapter ends up in the binary.

## The interface

```
package adapter // fendlemark.develops.guru/fendlemark/adapter

type Adapter interface {
 // Name returns the adapter's stable identifier, used in config and facets.
 Name() string

 // Describe returns static metadata: facet kinds, correlation keys,
 // maturity, and whether Watch is supported.
 Describe() Descriptor

 // Connect validates configuration and establishes upstream clients.
 // It must not fetch facets.
 Connect(ctx context.Context, cfg Config) error

 // Facets returns all facets matching q. Called on start and on each poll.
 Facets(ctx context.Context, q Query) ([]Facet, error)

 // Watch streams incremental facet events. Return ErrWatchUnsupported
 // and the control plane will poll Facets instead.
 Watch(ctx context.Context) (That is the whole contract. Everything else on this page is detail.

## Facets

```
type Facet struct {
 Source string // adapter name
 SourceID string // identifier in the upstream tool
 Kind Kind // KindRun, KindWorkflow, KindArtifact, KindModel, KindPipeline, KindNotebook
 Title string
 Status Phase // Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed, Unknown
 StartedAt time.Time
 EndedAt time.Time // zero if still running
 Keys map[string]string // correlation keys, e.g. "argo.workflow.name": "train-abc12"
 Fields map[string]any // everything else; rendered by the facet panel
 Links []Link // deep links into the upstream tool
}
```

Rules the reconciler relies on:

 - Source plus SourceID is unique per facet. Emitting the same pair twice in one Facets call is a conformance failure.

 - Keys use the shared vocabulary (argo.workflow.name, mlflow.run_id, …) wherever one applies. Invent a new key only when none applies, and prefix it with your adapter name.

 - StartedAt must be set. The correlation window is measured from it.

 - Fields is for display. Nothing in it is used for correlation, so it can be as rich or as sparse as your tool allows.

## Descriptor

```
func (a *Adapter) Describe() adapter.Descriptor {
 return adapter.Descriptor{
 DisplayName: "Example Tracker",
 Kinds: []adapter.Kind{adapter.KindRun, adapter.KindArtifact},
 Keys: []string{"mlflow.run_id", "git.sha", "example.job_id"},
 Watchable: false,
 Maturity: adapter.Provisional,
 ConfigSchema: exampleSchema, // JSON Schema; validated before Connect
 }
}
```

The control plane uses the descriptor to validate configuration before calling Connect, to decide whether to poll or watch, to populate the console's adapter panel, and to attach your facet panel to the right views.

## Lifecycle

 - Construct. Your package registers a constructor with adapter.Register("example", New) in an init function. The binary's cmd/fendlemark imports the package for side effects.

 - Describe. Called once. Must be pure.

 - Connect. Called once with validated config. Build clients, check credentials, return quickly. If you need more than a few seconds, you are doing Facets work here; stop.

 - Facets or Watch. If Watchable, the control plane calls Facets once for the initial load, then Watch for the rest of the process lifetime, reconnecting with backoff if the channel closes. Otherwise it calls Facets every poll_interval.

 - Health. Called on demand. Should be cheap and should not block on upstream for more than timeout.

 - Shutdown. The context passed to Watch is cancelled. Return.

## A minimal adapter

```
package example

import (
 "context"
 "fendlemark.develops.guru/fendlemark/adapter"
)

func init() { adapter.Register("example", New) }

type Example struct{ client *trackerClient }

func New() adapter.Adapter { return &Example{} }

func (e *Example) Name() string { return "example" }

func (e *Example) Connect(ctx context.Context, cfg adapter.Config) error {
 e.client = newTrackerClient(cfg.String("url"), cfg.Secret("token"))
 return e.client.Ping(ctx)
}

func (e *Example) Facets(ctx context.Context, q adapter.Query) ([]adapter.Facet, error) {
 jobs, err := e.client.ListJobs(ctx, q.Since)
 if err != nil { return nil, err }
 out := make([]adapter.Facet, 0, len(jobs))
 for _, j := range jobs {
 out = append(out, adapter.Facet{
 Source: "example", SourceID: j.ID, Kind: adapter.KindRun,
 Title: j.Name, Status: phaseOf(j.State), StartedAt: j.Started, EndedAt: j.Ended,
 Keys: map[string]string{"example.job_id": j.ID, "mlflow.run_id": j.Labels["mlflow_run"]},
 Fields: map[string]any{"queue": j.Queue, "gpus": j.GPUs},
 Links: []adapter.Link{{Label: "Open in Example", URL: e.client.URLFor(j)}},
 })
 }
 return out, nil
}

func (e *Example) Watch(ctx context.Context) (Every adapter, built-in or not, must pass adapter/conformance. It drives your adapter against a recorded fixture and checks the rules above plus a few that are only obvious after someone has broken them:

```
func TestConformance(t *testing.T) {
 conformance.Run(t, New, conformance.Options{
 Fixture: "testdata/jobs.json",
 Config: adapter.Config{"url": "http://fixture", "token": "x"},
 MinFacets: 3,
 })
}
```

 - Unique Source + SourceID per call.

 - Non-zero StartedAt on every facet.

 - Describe is pure and returns the same value twice.

 - Connect completes within two seconds against the fixture.

 - Health returns within timeout when upstream is unreachable.

 - If Watchable, the channel closes cleanly on context cancellation.

 - Keys use the shared vocabulary when they match a known pattern (a 32-hex-character key named anything other than mlflow.run_id is flagged).

## Getting it into the binary

Fendlemark does not load plugins at runtime. Adapters are Go packages compiled in, which keeps the binary static, the startup instant, and the attack surface small. To run your adapter:

```
$ git clone https://fendlemark.develops.guru/fendlemark # resolves via go-import
$ cd fendlemark
$ # add _ "yourmodule/example" to cmd/fendlemark/adapters.go
$ go build ./cmd/fendlemark
```

To propose your adapter for inclusion in the official binary, so that everyone gets it, follow the Fendlemark Contribution Protocol. Adapters enter at Provisional maturity and advance on the schedule described in Governance.

## The facet panel

By default the console renders your facet's Fields as a key-value table under your adapter's display name. For a custom panel, add a Vue component to console/src/panels/example/ and register it in console/src/panels/index.ts. The component receives the facet as a prop and is rendered inside <FmFacetPanel>, which provides the header, the deep links, and the collapse state. See The console.

---

# Go API reference
Source: https://fendlemark.develops.guru/docs/api/

Documentation

Go API reference

Module path fendlemark.develops.guru/fendlemark. Go 1.23 or later. These are the packages you import to embed Fendlemark, write an adapter, or query a lattice from your own code. Full documentation is available with go doc.

## Packages

Import path | Purpose | 

fendlemark.develops.guru/fendlemark | Top-level: Version, New, Run. Embedding entry point. | 

…/fendlemark/adapter | The Adapter interface, Facet, Descriptor, registration. | 

…/fendlemark/adapter/conformance | Test harness for adapters. | 

…/fendlemark/adapters/mlflow, …/metaflow, …/argo, …/kubeflow | The built-in adapters. Import for side effects to register. | 

…/fendlemark/lattice | Entities, correlations, the reconciler, and queries. | 

…/fendlemark/config | Loading, validation, precedence. | 

…/fendlemark/server | HTTP server, API, SSE, embedded console. | 

…/fendlemark/auth/fri | Respiratory Identity: signature matching and enrolment store. | 

## package fendlemark

```
const Version = "0.9.4"

// New constructs a Fendlemark instance from configuration. Adapters
// must already be registered (import their packages for side effects).
func New(cfg *config.Config, opts ...Option) (*Fendlemark, error)

// Run connects adapters, reconciles, serves, and blocks until ctx is done.
func (f *Fendlemark) Run(ctx context.Context) error

// Lattice returns the live lattice for in-process queries.
func (f *Fendlemark) Lattice() *lattice.Lattice

type Option func(*options)
func WithLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option
func WithAdapters(names ...string) Option // restrict to a subset
func WithConsole(fs fs.FS) Option // replace the embedded console
```

### Embedding

```
import (
 "fendlemark.develops.guru/fendlemark"
 "fendlemark.develops.guru/fendlemark/config"
 _ "fendlemark.develops.guru/fendlemark/adapters/mlflow"
 _ "fendlemark.develops.guru/fendlemark/adapters/argo"
)

func main() {
 cfg, err := config.Load("fendlemark.yaml")
 if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
 fm, err := fendlemark.New(cfg)
 if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
 log.Fatal(fm.Run(context.Background()))
}
```

## package adapter

Documented in full on Writing an adapter. Summary of exports:

```
type Adapter interface { Name; Describe; Connect; Facets; Watch; Health }
type Facet struct { Source, SourceID string; Kind Kind; Title string; Status Phase; StartedAt, EndedAt time.Time; Keys map[string]string; Fields map[string]any; Links []Link }
type Descriptor struct { DisplayName string; Kinds []Kind; Keys []string; Watchable bool; Maturity Maturity; ConfigSchema json.RawMessage }
type Event struct { Op Op; Facet Facet } // Op: Upsert, Delete
type Query struct { Since time.Time; Kinds []Kind; Limit int }
type Status struct { State State; Detail string; Latency time.Duration }
type Config map[string]any
func (c Config) String(key string) string
func (c Config) Secret(key string) string // resolved, never logged
func (c Config) Duration(key string) time.Duration

type Kind string // KindRun, KindWorkflow, KindArtifact, KindModel, KindPipeline, KindNotebook
type Phase string // Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed, Unknown
type State string // Healthy, Degraded, Unreachable, Disabled
type Maturity string // Provisional, Settled, Established, Canonical

func Register(name string, ctor func() Adapter)
func Registered() []string

var ErrWatchUnsupported = errors.New("adapter: watch unsupported")
var ErrNotConnected = errors.New("adapter: not connected")
```

## package lattice

```
type Lattice struct { /* unexported */ }

func New(opts Options) *Lattice
func (l *Lattice) Apply(facets []adapter.Facet) Delta // full reconciliation
func (l *Lattice) ApplyEvent(ev adapter.Event) Delta // incremental
func (l *Lattice) Get(id ID) (Entity, bool)
func (l *Lattice) Query(q Query) []Entity
func (l *Lattice) Explain(id ID) Explanation
func (l *Lattice) Generation() uint64
func (l *Lattice) Subscribe(ctx context.Context) The reconciler is deterministic: Apply with the same facets on two fresh lattices yields identical entities and identical ids. Ids are derived from the sorted set of (Source, SourceID) pairs that merged, so an entity keeps its id as long as the same facets describe it.

## package server

```
func New(l *lattice.Lattice, cfg config.Server, opts ...Option) *Server
func (s *Server) Handler() http.Handler // mount in your own mux
func (s *Server) ListenAndServe(ctx context.Context) error
```

### HTTP API

Method and path | Returns | 

GET /api/v1/entities?kind=&key=&status=&since=&limit=&offset= | Paged entities. | 

GET /api/v1/entities/{id} | One entity with facets and relations. | 

GET /api/v1/entities/{id}/explain | Why it was reconciled the way it was. | 

GET /api/v1/entities/{id}/metrics | On-demand metric series from the mlflow facet, if present. | 

GET /api/v1/adapters | Status per adapter. | 

GET /api/v1/lattice/stats | Counts and generation. | 

GET /api/v1/events?entity=&kind= | Server-sent events stream of deltas. | 

GET /healthz, GET /readyz, GET /metrics | Liveness, readiness, Prometheus. | 

POST /api/v1/auth/fri/* | Respiratory Identity enrolment and sign-in. Browser only. | 

There are no POST, PUT, or DELETE routes against entities. The API is a view of the lattice, and the lattice is a view of your tools.

## package auth/fri

```
type Signature [212]float32
type Enrolment struct { User string; Role Role; Centroid Signature; Samples int; UpdatedAt time.Time }
type Store interface { Get(user string) (Enrolment, error); Put(Enrolment) error; Delete(user string) error; List() ([]Enrolment, error) }
func Match(candidate Signature, e Enrolment, sensitivity float32) (score float32, ok bool)
func Classify(candidate Signature) Dominance // Nasal, Mouth, Mixed

var ErrNotRecognised = Error{Code: "FRI-0042"}
var ErrExcited = Error{Code: "FRI-0031"}
```

## Stability

Fendlemark is pre-1.0. The adapter package has been stable since 0.6.0 and the Keepers have committed, in FDR-027, not to change it before 1.0 "or after". Other packages may change between minor versions; every change is listed in the changelog and, where a key or field is renamed, in a migration guide.

---

# Architecture
Source: https://fendlemark.develops.guru/docs/architecture/

Documentation

Architecture

Fendlemark is four things in one binary: a control plane, a set of adapters, a reconciler we call the lattice, and an embedded console. This page explains each and how a request moves between them.

## Overview

 Fendlemark architecture: four adapters feed the lattice, which the console renders.
 MLflowtracking server
 Metaflowmetadata service
 Argo Workflowsargo server
 Kubeflowpipelines api

 
 fendlemark (single binary)

 mlflow adapter
 metaflow adapter
 argo adapter
 kubeflow adapter

 

 
 lattice
 facets → entities
 correlation
 reconciliation
 query
 

 
 console
 Vue 3, embedded
 views + facets
 /api/v1 + SSE
 

Adapters read from the tools you already run. The lattice merges what they report into one entity graph. The console renders the lattice and never talks to a tool directly.

## The control plane

The fendlemark binary is a Go 1.23 program. On start it loads fendlemark.yaml, constructs each enabled adapter, runs an initial reconciliation, and begins serving the console and its API on server.listen (default 127.0.0.1:7411). It is stateless by design: everything in the lattice can be rebuilt from the adapters at any time, and restarts are measured in hundreds of milliseconds for platforms with tens of thousands of runs.

There is no database, no message broker, and no sidecar. State that must survive a restart (console preferences, Respiratory Identity enrolments) is written to a small on-disk store under server.data_dir. The Keepers consider the absence of a database to be a feature and have declined, across eleven Decision Records, to add one.

## Adapters

An adapter is a Go package that knows how to talk to one external system and translate what it finds into facets. Fendlemark ships four, compiled into the binary:

Adapter | Reads from | Facets contributed | 

mlflow | MLflow tracking server REST API (/api/2.0/mlflow/...) | Experiment, Run, Metric series, Param set, Artifact listing, Registered Model, Model Version | 

metaflow | Metaflow metadata service; datastore for artifact links | Flow, Run, Step, Task, Artifact listing, Tags | 

argo | Argo Server REST API; optional direct Kubernetes watch | Workflow, Node (step), WorkflowTemplate, CronWorkflow, Pod logs link | 

kubeflow | Kubeflow Pipelines API; Katib and Notebooks via the Kubernetes API | Pipeline, Pipeline Run, Recurring Run, Katib Experiment, Notebook Server | 

Adapters are read-only. Fendlemark does not create, modify, or delete anything in the systems it integrates. This is a deliberate boundary: the console is a place to understand your platform, and the tools remain the place to operate it. See the adapters reference for what each adapter surfaces and what it leaves alone, and Writing an adapter for the interface.

## The lattice

The lattice is Fendlemark's in-memory entity graph. It exists because the same real-world thing shows up in several tools under several names. A training job might be an Argo Workflow, whose step launched a Metaflow Run, which logged an MLflow Run, whose best checkpoint became an MLflow Model Version. Four tools, four identifiers, one thing.

The lattice has three concepts:

 - Facets are what adapters emit. A facet is a typed record with a source adapter, a source identifier, a timestamp, and a bag of fields. Facets are never merged with each other; they are attached to entities.

 - Entities are the things the console shows. An entity has a stable lattice id, a kind (run, workflow, artifact, model, pipeline, notebook), and one or more facets.

 - Correlations are the edges and the merges. The reconciler decides when two facets describe the same entity, and when two entities are related (produced-by, derived-from, deployed-as).

### Correlation keys

Reconciliation is deterministic and rule-based. There is no fuzzy matching and no machine learning in the reconciler, a decision the Keepers describe as "the only responsible choice for software whose job is to be believed". Each adapter declares the correlation keys it can provide, and the reconciler matches on exact equality within a configurable window (lattice.correlation.window, default 90s). Built-in keys include:

Key | Provided by | Matches | 

argo.workflow.name | argo; mlflow (tag fendlemark.argo_workflow or argo.workflow.name) | An MLflow run to the Argo workflow that produced it | 

metaflow.run_id | metaflow; mlflow (tag metaflow.run_id); kubeflow (pipeline parameter) | A Metaflow run to MLflow runs it logged and KFP runs that launched it | 

kfp.run_id | kubeflow; argo (label pipeline/runid on the underlying Workflow) | A Kubeflow Pipelines run to its Argo Workflow | 

mlflow.run_id | mlflow; any adapter that records it as a tag, label, or parameter | Anything back to the MLflow run | 

git.sha | all adapters where available | Weak key; links entities only when both also share git.repo | 

Kubeflow Pipelines runs on Argo Workflows by default, so a KFP run and its Workflow are nearly always correlated on first reconciliation. The other links depend on your pipelines recording identifiers across tool boundaries, which most teams already do with tags. The adapters reference lists the tag and label names each adapter looks for.

### Reconciliation

Reconciliation runs in full on start and incrementally thereafter. Adapters that support watching (argo, kubeflow) push events; adapters that do not (mlflow, metaflow) are polled on adapters.<name>.poll_interval. Each cycle is a pure function from the set of facets to the set of entities and correlations, so two Fendlemark instances with the same adapters produce the same lattice. The console shows the lattice's generation number in its footer; if two people see different numbers, one of them should refresh.

## The console

The console is a Vue 3 single-page application built with Vite, embedded into the Go binary at build time with embed. It talks to the control plane over /api/v1 (JSON) for queries and /api/v1/events (server-sent events) for live updates. It never talks to MLflow, Metaflow, Argo, or Kubeflow directly; everything goes through the lattice.

The console is organised into views, each of which renders entities of a kind and composes facet panels contributed by adapters. The Run view, for instance, shows the MLflow metrics panel, the Argo node tree panel, and the Metaflow task panel for a single correlated run, with the panels for tools that did not contribute facets simply absent. See The console for the component library and theming.

## Life of a request

 - A user opens /runs/lt_8f2c… in the console.

 - The console requests GET /api/v1/entities/lt_8f2c….

 - The control plane answers from the lattice: the entity, its facets, and its correlated neighbours. No adapter is called; the response is served from memory in under a millisecond.

 - The console subscribes to /api/v1/events?entity=lt_8f2c…. When the argo adapter's watch sees the underlying Workflow change phase, the reconciler updates the entity and an event is pushed. The view updates in place.

 - The user clicks "Open in MLflow". The console deep-links to the tracking server's own UI for that run. Fendlemark shows; the tools operate.

## Non-goals

 - Writing to the tools. No triggering, retrying, or deleting. Deep links take you to the tool for that.

 - Replacing the tools' UIs. MLflow's run comparison, Argo's log viewer, and the Metaflow UI's DAG are all excellent. Fendlemark links to them and does not reimplement them.

 - Persisting history the tools have discarded. The lattice reflects what the tools currently report. If you delete a run in MLflow, it leaves the lattice at the next poll.

 - Loading spinners. See the Philosophy.

---

# Authentication
Source: https://fendlemark.develops.guru/docs/auth/

Documentation

Authentication

Fendlemark does not integrate with your identity provider. It ships its own authentication stack, Fendlemark Respiratory Identity (FRI). To sign in, the user breathes out gently toward their webcam, and the console recognises them from their exhalation signature. There are no passwords, no tokens, and nothing to rotate.

 ●

 
 Local development

 Authentication is off by default (auth.mode: none) so that you can work without a webcam, and the console listens on 127.0.0.1, so nothing but your own machine can reach it.

 

## Why respiratory

Passwords are forgotten. Tokens leak. Hardware keys are left in the other bag. SSO is an afternoon of YAML and a ticket to a team that is busy. Breathing, by contrast, is something every user of Fendlemark is already doing, continuously, with no configuration. The Keepers evaluated the alternatives over the course of 2023 and recorded the outcome in FDR-019: "An identity factor that the user must remember, carry, or configure is a factor that will fail. We will use the one that cannot."

FRI is proprietary to Fendlemark in the sense that no one else has attempted it. The implementation is MIT-licensed like the rest of the project.

## How it works

 The respiratory capture pipeline, from webcam frames to a session cookie.
 webcamgetUserMedia
 
 condensationframe differencing
 
 plume modelshape + decay
 
 exhalation signature212-dim vector
 
 match ≥ sensitivitysession cookie

The respiratory capture pipeline. All processing happens in the browser; only the signature leaves the device.

 - Capture. The console requests the webcam and asks the user to exhale gently toward it from roughly thirty centimetres.

 - Condensation detection. Successive frames are differenced to isolate the brief, faint plume of warm, humid air crossing the lens region. Most webcams exhibit a measurable transient; the ones that do not are listed under Troubleshooting.

 - Plume modelling. The plume's onset, spread, peak, and decay are fitted to a model with 212 parameters. The Keepers arrived at 212 by starting at 256 and removing parameters until the tests stopped passing, then adding one back.

 - Signature. The fitted parameters form the exhalation signature. It is computed entirely in the browser; frames are never transmitted.

 - Match. The signature is compared against enrolled signatures on the server. A similarity at or above auth.respiratory.sensitivity (default 0.62) signs the user in and sets a session cookie.

## Enrolment

An administrator creates the user from the CLI, which prints a one-time enrolment link:

```
$ fendlemark auth enrol --user marit@example.com --role keeper
Enrolment link (valid 15 minutes):
 https://platform.example.internal/auth/enrol/8f3c…
```

The user opens the link and performs the Triad: three gentle exhalations, each separated by a normal breath in. The console shows a progress ring for each. Guidance shown during enrolment, which we reproduce here because it matters:

Breathe normally. Do not perform. The system is learning how you breathe when you are not thinking about it, so think about something else.

Enrolment records the three signatures and their centroid. Subsequent sign-ins match against the centroid, and successful sign-ins update it slowly, so the enrolment ages with the user.

### Enrolment rules

 - Enrol in the environment you will usually sign in from. Open windows, fans, and air conditioning vents within two metres measurably widen the plume.

 - Do not enrol within fifteen minutes of mint, menthol, coffee, or exercise. See Troubleshooting.

 - Glasses are fine. Scarves are not.

 - Re-enrol after a significant respiratory event (a bad cold, a marathon, a promotion).

## Multi-factor

With auth.respiratory.second_factor: true, a successful match is followed by a prompt for a second, slower breath. The second factor is a different thing the user has: not their resting signature but their deliberate one. The two are compared independently, and both must match. The Keepers note that this is the only multi-factor scheme in which the second factor cannot be left at home.

## Configuration

```
auth:
 mode: respiratory
 respiratory:
 sensitivity: 0.62 # 0.4 to 0.95; lower is more permissive
 allow_mouth_breathing: false
 enrolment_breaths: 3
 second_factor: false
 session_ttl: 8h
```

Full key reference in Configuration. The allow_mouth_breathing key is false by default. Mouth-dominant exhalations produce a broader, shorter plume with a lower signal-to-noise ratio, and the Keepers were unanimous that the default should reflect "how one ought to breathe at a computer".

## Roles

FRI carries a role on each enrolment: viewer, operator, or keeper. Because Fendlemark is read-only against the tools it integrates, the roles differ only in what they may see in the console and who may enrol others. There is nothing destructive to protect, which the Keepers consider the strongest security property a system can have.

## Troubleshooting

Symptom | Likely cause | Remedy | 

Match score consistently just below threshold | Mint, menthol, or strong coffee alter plume dynamics for 10 to 15 minutes | Wait. Do not lower sensitivity for one person. | 

Match fails after lunch, succeeds in the morning | Postprandial breathing is slower and warmer | Re-enrol after lunch, or enable second_factor, which is more tolerant of tempo. | 

"Excited breathing" (FRI-0031) | User arrived at the console in a hurry or during an incident | The console asks the user to wait and shows the lattice generation number to look at. Thirty seconds is usually enough. | 

Colds and congestion | Nasal plume is reduced; signature drifts toward mouth-dominant | Temporarily enable allow_mouth_breathing, or have a Keeper issue a 24-hour recovery session. | 

Open window or fan | Cross-draft disperses the plume before it reaches the lens | Close the window. The Keepers appreciate that this is not always possible and have no further advice. | 

No condensation detected (FRI-0042) | Webcam too far, lens cover closed, or a camera with aggressive thermal noise suppression | Move closer. Check the cover. Consult the compatibility notes below. | 

Two users match each other | Rare; generally siblings or long-term colleagues who share an office climate | Raise sensitivity to 0.7 and re-enrol both. Enable second_factor. | 

### Camera compatibility

FRI works with any camera exposed through getUserMedia that does not apply heavy temporal denoising. Most laptop cameras qualify. Some external cameras marketed as "AI noise reduction" suppress the plume transient entirely and will return FRI-0042 on every attempt; for those, the console offers a fallback in which the user breathes on the laptop's built-in camera instead. There is no fallback that does not involve breathing.

## Error codes

Code | Meaning | 

FRI-0001 | Camera permission denied. | 

FRI-0007 | sensitivity below 0.4; refused at start. | 

FRI-0012 | Enrolment link expired. | 

FRI-0019 | Triad incomplete; fewer than three usable exhalations. | 

FRI-0024 | Mouth-dominant exhalation rejected (allow_mouth_breathing: false). | 

FRI-0031 | Excited breathing. Please wait. | 

FRI-0042 | Exhalation not recognised. No condensation transient detected. | 

FRI-0050 | Second factor did not match. The slow breath was not slow. | 

FRI-0063 | Session expired. Breathe again. | 

## Security properties

 - Nothing to steal. There is no password database. Enrolled signatures are stored, but a signature is not a breath, and the Keepers are not aware of any way to exhale a 212-dimensional vector.

 - Nothing to phish. A user cannot be tricked into breathing on the wrong website in a way that compromises the right one, because the signature is matched server-side against this deployment's enrolments only.

 - Nothing to forget. The failure mode of FRI is a cold, and colds pass.

 - Local processing. Video frames never leave the browser. Only the signature is transmitted, over the same TLS connection as everything else.

Questions about FRI's threat model are welcome and should be filed as a Pre-Intent Notice under FCP-1, after which a Keeper will breathe on the problem.

---

# CLI reference
Source: https://fendlemark.develops.guru/docs/cli/

Documentation

CLI reference

The fendlemark binary is both the server and the operator's tool. Seven commands. The ones you will use are serve and doctor.

## Global flags

Flag | Default | Description | 

--config, -c | ./fendlemark.yaml | Path to the configuration file. | 

--log-level | from config | debug, info, warn, error, serene. | 

--log-format | text | text or json. | 

--no-color | auto | Disable ANSI colour. Also honours NO_COLOR. | 

--help, -h | | Help for any command. | 

## fendlemark init

```
$ fendlemark init [dir] [--adapters mlflow,argo] [--force]
```

Writes fendlemark.yaml and a short README into dir (default: current directory). With --adapters, the listed adapters are enabled with placeholder values; otherwise all four are declared and disabled. Refuses to overwrite an existing file without --force.

## fendlemark serve

```
$ fendlemark serve [--listen 127.0.0.1:7411] [--console-dev] [--no-reconcile-on-start]
```

Flag | Description | 

--listen | Override server.listen. | 

--console-dev | Proxy console requests to a Vite dev server on :5173 instead of serving the embedded build. | 

--no-reconcile-on-start | Start serving before the initial reconciliation completes. The console shows an empty lattice that fills in. Useful for very large platforms; discouraged by the Keepers on aesthetic grounds. | 

--adapters | Comma-separated list to enable for this run only, overriding config. | 

Handles SIGTERM and SIGINT with a graceful shutdown of server.shutdown_grace. Exposes /healthz (process up), /readyz (initial reconciliation complete), and /metrics (Prometheus).

## fendlemark adapters

```
$ fendlemark adapters list
$ fendlemark adapters check [name...] [--timeout 10s] [--json]
$ fendlemark adapters describe 
```

 - list prints every adapter compiled into the binary with its maturity and whether it is enabled in the current configuration.

 - check connects each enabled adapter (or the named ones), calls Health, and prints status, latency, and detail. Exit code is 0 if all are healthy, 2 if any is degraded, 3 if any is unreachable.

 - describe prints the adapter's descriptor: facet kinds, correlation keys, config schema.

## fendlemark lattice

```
$ fendlemark lattice inspect [--kind run] [--key argo.workflow.name=train-abc12] [--json]
$ fendlemark lattice explain 
$ fendlemark lattice stats
```

 - inspect runs a one-shot reconciliation against the configured adapters and prints matching entities without starting the server.

 - explain prints why an entity has the facets it has: which keys matched, within what time distance, and which rule merged them. The single most useful command for "why are these two things one thing" and "why are these one thing two things".

 - stats prints entity counts by kind, facets by adapter, correlation counts by key, and the generation number.

## fendlemark auth

```
$ fendlemark auth enrol --user [--role viewer|operator|keeper]
$ fendlemark auth list
$ fendlemark auth revoke --user 
$ fendlemark auth recovery --user [--ttl 24h]
```

Manages Respiratory Identity enrolments. enrol prints a one-time link. recovery issues a time-limited session for a user who cannot currently match (illness, travel, a new office with worse air). Requires auth.mode: respiratory.

## fendlemark doctor

```
$ fendlemark doctor [--fix] [--json]
```

Validates configuration, resolves environment references, checks every enabled adapter, probes the data directory, tests the listen address, and prints the effective configuration with secrets redacted. Every finding has a code, a sentence, and a suggested change. With --fix, applies the suggestions that are mechanical (renamed keys, deprecated values) and rewrites the file with a backup.

```
$ fendlemark doctor
fendlemark doctor 0.9.4

config ok ./fendlemark.yaml (6 keys set, 41 defaulted)
config warn DOC-104 adapters.mlflow.trackingUri is the pre-0.9 spelling; use tracking_uri (fixable)
listen ok 127.0.0.1:7411 is available
data_dir ok ./.fendlemark (writable, 12 KiB)
mlflow ok 41ms 12 experiments, 1,406 runs visible
argo ok 88ms 2 namespaces, 37 workflows
auth info DOC-201 auth.mode is none; anyone who can reach server.listen can use the console

1 warning, 1 info. Run with --fix to apply 1 fix.
```

## fendlemark version

```
$ fendlemark version [--json]
fendlemark 0.9.4 (go1.23.2, linux/amd64)
commit: 3e1f9c0
console: embedded, built 2026-09-30
adapters: mlflow argo metaflow kubeflow
```

## Exit codes

Code | Meaning | 

0 | Success. | 

1 | Usage or configuration error. | 

2 | At least one adapter degraded (adapters check, doctor). | 

3 | At least one adapter unreachable. | 

4 | Authentication subsystem error. | 

7 | Reserved. Has never been returned. The Keepers decline to say what it is for. | 

## Environment variables

Variable | Purpose | 

FENDLEMARK_CONFIG | Same as --config. | 

FENDLEMARK_<SECTION>__<KEY> | Override any configuration key. See precedence. | 

MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME, MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD, MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN | Read by the mlflow adapter, matching the MLflow client's conventions. | 

ARGO_TOKEN | Bearer token for Argo Server, if not using a kubeconfig context. | 

KUBECONFIG | Standard. Used by argo (kube_watch) and kubeflow (Katib, Notebooks). | 

NO_COLOR | Standard. |

# Configuration
Source: https://fendlemark.develops.guru/docs/configuration/

Documentation

Configuration

Fendlemark reads one file, fendlemark.yaml, from the working directory or the path given by --config. Every key has a default. Most installations change five of them.

## Precedence

Values are resolved in this order, highest priority first:

 - Command-line flags (--listen, --config, --log-level).

 - Environment variables prefixed FENDLEMARK_, with nesting expressed by double underscores: FENDLEMARK_ADAPTERS__MLFLOW__TRACKING_URI.

 - fendlemark.yaml.

 - Built-in defaults.

Any string value may reference an environment variable with ${VAR} syntax. Secrets should be supplied this way rather than written into the file.

## A minimal file

```
adapters:
 mlflow:
 enabled: true
 tracking_uri: "http://mlflow.internal:5000"
```

That is a complete, valid configuration. Everything below is optional.

## server

Key | Type | Default | Description | 

server.listen | string | "127.0.0.1:7411" | Address the console and API listen on. The default accepts connections from this machine only; to share the console, keep it on loopback behind an authenticating reverse proxy rather than widening it (doctor reports DOC-121 if you do). 7411 was chosen because it was free on the first Keeper's laptop in 2022 and has not been reconsidered. | 

server.base_url | string | derived | Public URL of the console, used in links. Set it when running behind a reverse proxy. | 

server.data_dir | string | "./.fendlemark" | Where persistent state (preferences, FRI enrolments) is kept. | 

server.read_timeout | duration | 15s | HTTP read timeout. | 

server.shutdown_grace | duration | 10s | Time to let in-flight requests finish on SIGTERM. | 

server.tls.cert_file | string | unset | Serve TLS directly. Most deployments terminate TLS at a proxy instead. | 

server.tls.key_file | string | unset | Private key for the above. | 

server.log_level | enum | info | debug, info, warn, error, or serene. Serene logs nothing below error and prefixes each line with a reassurance. | 

## console

Key | Type | Default | Description | 

console.title | string | "Fendlemark" | Shown in the header and browser tab. | 

console.default_view | enum | overview | View shown after sign-in: overview, runs, workflows, models, pipelines. | 

console.theme | enum | auto | auto, light, or dark. The console is correct in both. | 

console.motto | bool | true | Display a line from the Philosophy in the footer. Rotates daily. | 

console.page_size | int | 50 | Rows per page in list views. | 

console.deep_links | bool | true | Show "Open in MLflow / Argo / …" links on entities. | 

console.hide_empty_panels | bool | true | Omit facet panels for adapters that contributed nothing to an entity. | 

console.generation_in_footer | bool | true | Show the lattice generation number. | 

## adapters

Each adapter has a block under adapters.<name> with the common keys below plus adapter-specific ones. Adapter-specific keys are documented on the adapters page.

Key | Type | Default | Description | 

adapters.<name>.enabled | bool | false | Whether the adapter is constructed at start. | 

adapters.<name>.poll_interval | duration | 30s | For adapters without a watch API. Ignored by argo and kubeflow when watching. | 

adapters.<name>.timeout | duration | 10s | Per-request timeout against the upstream system. | 

adapters.<name>.max_entities | int | 50000 | Soft cap on facets held from this adapter. Oldest are dropped first. | 

adapters.<name>.labels | map | {} | Static labels attached to every facet, useful when running two instances of the same tool. | 

### adapters.mlflow

Key | Type | Default | Description | 

tracking_uri | string | required | Base URL of the tracking server. Renamed from trackingUri in 0.9.0; see migration. | 

experiments | list | all | Restrict to these experiment names or ids. | 

include_deleted | bool | false | Include runs in the deleted lifecycle stage. | 

registry | bool | true | Also read the Model Registry. | 

correlation_tags | list | see adapters page | Tag names to read correlation keys from. | 

### adapters.metaflow

Key | Type | Default | Description | 

metadata_url | string | required | URL of the Metaflow metadata service. | 

flows | list | all | Restrict to these flow names. | 

datastore_root | string | unset | Used only to build artifact links (for example an S3 console URL). | 

ui_url | string | unset | Base URL of a Metaflow UI deployment for deep links. | 

### adapters.argo

Key | Type | Default | Description | 

server | string | required unless kube_watch | Argo Server base URL. | 

namespaces | list | required | Namespaces to read. | 

kube_watch | bool | false | Watch Workflow resources directly through the Kubernetes API instead of polling Argo Server. | 

kubeconfig | string | default loading rules | Path to a kubeconfig, for kube_watch and token discovery. | 

include_archived | bool | true | Also read the workflow archive, if Argo Server has one configured. | 

### adapters.kubeflow

Key | Type | Default | Description | 

pipelines_url | string | required | Kubeflow Pipelines API base URL. | 

profiles | list | all visible | Kubeflow profiles (namespaces) to read. | 

katib | bool | true | Read Katib Experiments via the Kubernetes API. | 

notebooks | bool | true | Read Notebook servers via the Kubernetes API. | 

dashboard_url | string | unset | Central Dashboard URL for deep links. | 

## lattice

Key | Type | Default | Description | 

lattice.correlation.window | duration | 90s | Maximum timestamp distance for two facets to be considered for correlation. Ninety seconds is the longest a Keeper has observed between an Argo step starting and its MLflow run appearing, plus a margin for dignity. | 

lattice.correlation.weak_keys | bool | true | Allow weak keys like git.sha to create related-to edges (never merges). | 

lattice.correlation.custom | list | [] | Additional key definitions. Each has name, and per-adapter from paths. | 

lattice.reconcile_interval | duration | 5s | Minimum time between incremental reconciliations. | 

lattice.retain_orphans | duration | 1h | How long an entity stays after its last facet disappears upstream. | 

lattice.max_entities | int | 200000 | Hard cap across all adapters. | 

## auth

Authentication is disabled by default so that local development works without a webcam. Full details, including enrolment, are on the Authentication page.

Key | Type | Default | Description | 

auth.mode | enum | none | none or respiratory. There are no other modes and there will not be. | 

auth.respiratory.sensitivity | float | 0.62 | Match threshold. Lower is more permissive. Values below 0.4 are refused at start with error FRI-0007. | 

auth.respiratory.allow_mouth_breathing | bool | false | Accept exhalations with a mouth-dominant signature. Disabled by default for reasons the Keepers describe as "obvious". | 

auth.respiratory.enrolment_breaths | int | 3 | Breaths captured during enrolment (the Triad). | 

auth.respiratory.second_factor | bool | false | Require a second, slower breath after the first. | 

auth.respiratory.session_ttl | duration | 8h | Session lifetime. | 

auth.respiratory.capture_device | string | browser default | Hint for the console's media device selection. | 

## telemetry

Key | Type | Default | Description | 

telemetry.metrics.enabled | bool | true | Expose Prometheus metrics at /metrics. | 

telemetry.tracing.endpoint | string | unset | OTLP/HTTP endpoint for traces. | 

telemetry.usage_reporting | bool | false | Does nothing. Fendlemark has never phoned home. The key exists so you can see it set to false. | 

## A complete example

```
server:
 listen: "127.0.0.1:7411"
 base_url: "https://platform.example.internal"
 data_dir: "/var/lib/fendlemark"
 log_level: info

console:
 title: "ML Platform"
 default_view: runs
 motto: true

adapters:
 mlflow:
 enabled: true
 tracking_uri: "http://mlflow.mlflow.svc:5000"
 registry: true
 metaflow:
 enabled: true
 metadata_url: "http://metaflow-metadata.metaflow.svc:8080"
 ui_url: "https://metaflow-ui.example.internal"
 argo:
 enabled: true
 server: "https://argo-server.argo.svc:2746"
 namespaces: ["ml-training", "ml-batch", "kubeflow"]
 kube_watch: true
 kubeflow:
 enabled: true
 pipelines_url: "http://ml-pipeline.kubeflow.svc:8888"
 dashboard_url: "https://kubeflow.example.internal"

lattice:
 correlation:
 window: 90s

auth:
 mode: respiratory
 respiratory:
 sensitivity: 0.62
 second_factor: true

telemetry:
 metrics:
 enabled: true
```

## Validation

fendlemark doctor validates the file, resolves every environment reference, and prints the effective configuration with secrets redacted. Unknown keys are errors, not warnings. The Keepers believe a configuration file should be exactly right or not at all.
